newsitem.title: USA: Alaska sled-dog race board member ousted for deaths.
newsitem.headline: Alaska sled-dog race board member ousted for deaths.

text.p: A board member of the Yukon Quest International Sled Dog Race was ousted from his position after inspectors found dead and underfed animals on his Fairbanks, Alaska, dog lot, race officials said on Tuesday.
Randy Emmet was removed from the race's board of directors on Friday, a day after animal control officers seized 11 dead dogs and 14 overly thin dogs from his lot, Quest spokesman Gus Lindquist said.
Emmett, who blamed a virus for the deaths, said he could not afford to pay for veterinarian care, Lindquist said.
Other board members, the race's executive director and others involved in the race were "appalled" at that explanation, Lindquist said.

The Quest opened a hotline over the weekend to aid dog owners who might be having trouble taking care of their animals. The dog-care hotline was already in the works before Emmett's problems were discovered, Lindquist said.
"We don't want anybody to feel that they can use that excuse, that they didn't have the resources to properly care for their dogs," he said.
Some animal welfare groups have criticised long-distance sled-dog racing, Lindquist said.
The Yukon Quest runs 1,000 miles (1,609 km) between Whitehorse, Yukon Territory, and Fairbanks, Alaska. The race started on Saturday in Whitehorse. Two dogs have already died in the race.
Emmett, a former executive director of the Yukon Quest, faces possible cruelty charges.
